jobs.title: Head of Market Intelligence & Analytics
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Northland, we’re enablers of change, united by our journey to transform the energy sector into the foundation for a sustainable future.

Since our inception, we’ve been early movers in the energy industry, adopting new initiatives that pave the way for communities across the globe and helping forge their path towards a carbon-neutral landscape.

We’re a different kind of independent power producer. As developers, owners and operators who are at the forefront of the energy transition, we’re uniquely positioned to leave a lasting impact in the regions where we operate. We’ve expanded our business across Canada, the United States, Latin America, Europe and Asia to become a global leader, all by bringing together industry experts to find solutions with an entrepreneurial mindset.

While our work powers communities across the globe, Northland is powered by our people.

What You’ll Do

The Head of Market Intelligence & Analytics is accountable for building and leading Northland’s enterprise market intelligence and analytics capabilities. The role establishes independent, decision-ready views of wholesale power and related commodity markets, translates those views into consistent commercial assumptions, and ensures those insights are applied across strategy, development, M&A, financing, market operations, asset management and portfolio optimization.

Establish scalable in-house forecasting and modelling capabilities, guide market analysts and technical resources, and determine where external specialists remain appropriate. The successful candidate combines deep electricity-market judgment, strong quantitative fluency, practical model-development oversight and the ability to communicate complex market dynamics to executive and investment audiences.

Build a global centre of expertise that protects, optimizes and sustainably grows the commercial value of Northland’s contracted and merchant portfolio, while underpinning new development opportunities with rigorous market intelligence, forward curves, fundamental analysis, scenario modelling and asset-level commercial insight. The initial priority is to establish repeatable capabilities for core markets and then scale them across Northland’s broader international portfolio.

The role is required to work in the Toronto office 4 days per week with one flexible day to work from home.

Key Responsibilities

Market Intelligence

Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, lead the development of Northland’s wholesale market strategy across relevant jurisdictions, identifying long-term trends, structural opportunities, downside risks and implications for capital allocation.
Develop and maintain internal views on supply and demand evolution, market design, natural gas, carbon, capacity, ancillary services, environmental attributes and other material value drivers.
Create a consistent market-outlook and assumption-setting process for use across business cases, investment decisions, budgets, forecasts and commercial strategies.
Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, translate market, policy and regulatory developments into alerts and actionable recommendations for internal stakeholders.

Forecasting, Modelling and Analytics

Own the roadmap and delivery of internal forward curves (short and long term), market-level fundamental models and supporting analytical tools, beginning with priority markets and scaling as business needs and capability mature.
Set modelling architecture, scenarios, input assumptions and quality standards; provide sufficient technical depth to review, challenge and guide Python-based and commercial-platform model development.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analysis covering load growth, generation additions and retirements, fuel and carbon prices, weather, transmission build-out, policy, technology costs, capture rates and operating constraints.
Build dashboards and repeatable reporting that make market views, assumptions, risks and forecast changes transparent and accessible to decision-makers.

Asset, Portfolio and Transaction Decision Support

Lead market analysis supporting development, acquisitions, divestitures, financing, budgeting and optimization of operating assets, including merchant revenue forecasts and high-level asset valuations.
Provide dispatch, capture-price, congestion, basis, curtailment, ancillary-service and other commercial analyses appropriate to each market, technology and contract structure.
Support hedging decisions, PPA and offtake strategy, competitive bid and RFP analysis, route-to-market decisions, commercial operating strategies and portfolio risk discussions.
Partner with Finance and transaction teams on lender, sale and investment processes, using independent third-party forecasts where external validation is required while maintaining a clear Northland view.

Capability, Data and Model Governance

Establish a practical build-versus-buy strategy for data, tools, modelling platforms and external advisory support, with clear accountabilities, budgets and service standards.
Implement model governance covering documentation, version control, assumption ownership, change management, validation, back-testing [CS3.1]and independent challenge proportionate to the decision being supported.
Define data requirements and partner with Technical Performance Management, Data, Digital and IT teams to develop reliable and scalable market-data infrastructure.
Manage relationships with market-data providers, modelling vendors and consultants; reduce avoidable external dependence while retaining specialist support where it adds value or is required by third parties.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnerships

Build, lead and develop a high-performing market intelligence and analytics team, setting priorities and balancing recurring market coverage with transaction and asset-specific demands.
Act as a senior thought partner to Development, Regulatory & Market Affairs, Government Affairs, Asset Management, Risk, Finance and executive leadership.
Present complex market conclusions, model limitations and key uncertainties in a clear, decision-oriented manner for investment committees, senior leaders and boards.

Who You Are

A strategic market leader: You possess deep expertise in wholesale power and commodity markets and can translate market trends, risks and opportunities into commercial strategy, investment decisions and portfolio outcomes. 
An analytical and technically credible expert: You combine strong quantitative capabilities with hands-on experience in market modelling, forecasting and data analytics, bringing the ability to challenge assumptions, interrogate models and drive rigorous decision-making. 
A builder of capabilities: You thrive in creating and scaling new functions, frameworks and governance models, balancing internal capability development with the strategic use of external tools, data and advisory support. 
A trusted advisor and communicator: You can distill complex market dynamics, forecasts and uncertainties into clear, actionable insights that influence executives, investment committees and boards. 
A collaborative and inspiring leader: You build high-performing teams, foster technical excellence and partner effectively across functions, geographies and stakeholder groups to deliver business value. 

Qualifications And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in economics, engineering, mathematics, statistics, finance, computer science or a related discipline; a relevant master’s degree or MBA is an asset.
10 or more years of progressive experience in wholesale power markets, energy-market analytics, fundamental forecasting, commercial strategy or a closely related field, including leadership of people or major analytical programs.
Demonstrated experience developing or directing power-market forecasts, fundamental models, dispatch and revenue analysis, scenario frameworks and asset-valuation inputs.
Deep understanding of electricity-market design and commercial drivers; experience across more than one ISO/RTO or international market is strongly preferred.
Experience across a diverse technology portfolio, such as wind, solar, storage and gas-fired generation, and with contracted and merchant revenue structures.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, manage external advisors and convert complex analytical work into clear commercial decisions.

What’s In It for You:

Our employees are the driving force behind our achievements. We are unwavering in our commitment to not only recognise your contributions but also to empower
you to excel in every aspect of your life. Here's a glimpse of why Northland is the place where you'll truly thrive: 

Thoughtful benefits – A competitive RRSP matching scheme of 8%; extended health, dental and vision benefits for yourself and your immediate family from day one; paid parental leave; Accident and Life Insurance and disability benefits are just a few of the benefits you’ll be able to access. 
Wellbeing first – Staying true to our taking care of ourselves and each other value, you will have access to our global Wellness Program and Employee Assistance Program, including access to mental health resources. 
Floating days and Birthdays off – As part of our commitment to promoting a healthy work-life balance, you will get your birthday off so you can celebrate however you choose! You will also receive three additional days off annually to observe any other events that are important to you.

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we still encourage you to apply. Learn more about our diversity, inclusion and belonging commitments.

Pay Range

$173,600.00 - $217,000.00

About UJA Federation of Greater Toronto

At UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, our vision is to lead the most vibrant Jewish community in North America - a community characterized by its diversity, unity, compassion, generosity and commitment to Jewish values. Together with our philanthropic, volunteer and professional leadership, we’re changing lives.
As one of North America’s leading Jewish non-profits, UJA Federation of Greater Toronto works to preserve and strengthen the quality of Jewish life in Greater Toronto, Canada, Israel and around the world. UJA advances this mission through fundraising, programs, and research focused on our strategic pillars: fighting poverty and improving well-being, growing Jewish education and identity, countering antisemitism and hate, and strengthening connections with Israel and Jewish communities worldwide.
About the Opportunity

The team is looking to amplify and strengthen our fundraising strategy. As part of this initiative, we are hiring an Associate Director, Data Analytics & Prospecting
to own UJA's donor intelligence ecosystem — driving the data strategy, prospecting vision, and analytical frameworks that equip leadership, frontline fundraisers and operational teams with the intelligence they need to deepen cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and campaign performance across the organization. Reporting to the Senior Director of Data, Analytics and Reporting, this role serves as the operational lead to the Senior Director within the function and acts as delegate to the Senior Director when needed.
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Influence
Own and evolve UJA's end-to-end donor intelligence ecosystem, encompassing analytics strategy, prospect identification, data governance, and performance measurement.
Serve as a strategic operational lead alongside the Senior Director, driving the vision and roadmap for how data and prospecting power UJA's fundraising goals.
Act as delegate to the Senior Director in their absence, representing the function to senior leadership and ensuring continuity of strategic priorities.
Drive organization-wide decisions by translating donor intelligence into fundraising strategy — influencing campaign planning, gift officer deployment, portfolio design, and solicitation priorities.
Present insights, strategic recommendations, and performance reporting to executive leadership, and key stakeholders across the organization.
Champion a data-driven culture across the Integrated Development division, shaping how teams think about and use donor intelligence in their work.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Impact
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of two direct reports, fostering analytical excellence, professional growth, and high performance.
Spearhead cross-functional initiatives with Research, IT/Salesforce, Marketing, and frontline fundraising teams to embed analytics and prospecting insights into day-to-day operations.
Build and strengthen collaborative partnerships with senior fundraisers and division leaders, serving as a trusted advisor on donor strategy, capacity analysis, and prospect prioritization.
Establish and continuously improve standards, workflows, and best practices that scale the function's impact across the organization.

Donor Analytics & Performance Accountability
Design and own predictive models, donor scoring methodologies, and segmentation strategies that directly contribute to pipeline growth, major gift acquisition, and campaign performance targets.
Develop and maintain executive-level dashboards and reporting that connect analytics outputs to fundraising outcomes — tracking prospect conversion, portfolio health, upgrade rates, and campaign progress.
Deliver strategic portfolio and capacity analysis that equips operational teams with the intelligence they need to optimize fundraiser assignments, close capacity gaps, and act on high-potential upgrade and re-engagement opportunities.
Establish the KPIs and success metrics that hold the donor intelligence function accountable to fundraising impact, and ensure the resulting data sets are delivered to the operations team to inform execution and performance tracking
Evaluate and implement emerging technologies, including AI and automation, to deepen donor intelligence capabilities and accelerate prospecting at scale.
Establish and enforce data quality standards and governance practices to ensure accuracy and integrity across all systems and outputs.

Prospect Strategy & Pipeline Development
Set the strategic direction for prospect research and identification, ensuring the function proactively feeds the major gifts and campaign pipeline with qualified, high-value prospects.
Oversee the delivery of timely, high-quality research profiles, briefings, and due diligence that enable senior fundraisers to engage with confidence.
Drive innovation in prospect identification through wealth screening, data mining, predictive analytics, and community network analysis.
Develop and refine prospecting policies, processes, and frameworks that support the Integrated Development division's growth objectives.

Qualifications:

Relevant education or equivalent experience.
7+ years of progressive experience in fundraising analytics, prospect research, data strategy, or nonprofit development, with increasing strategic leadership responsibility.
3+ years of experience managing, mentoring, and developing staff, with demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence beyond direct reports.
Passionate advocate and visible champion of UJA’s mission, values, and goals, inspiring others through action and unwavering commitment to advancing our shared purpose.
Proven track record of driving fundraising outcomes through data — not just delivering reports, but shaping strategy and influencing organizational decisions.
Deep expertise in predictive modeling, donor scoring, portfolio segmentation, and performance measurement frameworks.
Proficient with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) and experienced working with large, complex datasets.
Strong understanding of AI and emerging technologies, with a track record of implementing tools that drive efficiency and strategic advantage.
Executive-level communication and presentation skills, with comfort presenting to senior leadership, and key stakeholders across the organization.
Familiarity with donor intelligence and wealth screening platforms such as iWave or similar tools.
Actively engaged in, and/or familiar with groups, networks, or organizations in the Jewish community, with the ability to engage, build relationships, and surface potential new donor prospects.
Strong project management skills with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational demands.
Maintains a high degree of discretion, confidentiality, and respect for donor privacy.

This is a full-time permanent position, Salary Range: $89,000-99,000 annually, based on experience.

Who We Are

At Northland, we’re enablers of change, united by our journey to transform the energy sector into the foundation for a sustainable future.

Since our inception, we’ve been early movers in the energy industry, adopting new initiatives that pave the way for communities across the globe and helping forge their path towards a carbon-neutral landscape.

We’re a different kind of independent power producer. As developers, owners and operators who are at the forefront of the energy transition, we’re uniquely positioned to leave a lasting impact in the regions where we operate. We’ve expanded our business across Canada, the United States, Latin America, Europe and Asia to become a global leader, all by bringing together industry experts to find solutions with an entrepreneurial mindset.

While our work powers communities across the globe, Northland is powered by our people.

What You’ll Do

The Head of Market Intelligence & Analytics is accountable for building and leading Northland’s enterprise market intelligence and analytics capabilities. The role establishes independent, decision-ready views of wholesale power and related commodity markets, translates those views into consistent commercial assumptions, and ensures those insights are applied across strategy, development, M&A, financing, market operations, asset management and portfolio optimization.

Establish scalable in-house forecasting and modelling capabilities, guide market analysts and technical resources, and determine where external specialists remain appropriate. The successful candidate combines deep electricity-market judgment, strong quantitative fluency, practical model-development oversight and the ability to communicate complex market dynamics to executive and investment audiences.

Build a global centre of expertise that protects, optimizes and sustainably grows the commercial value of Northland’s contracted and merchant portfolio, while underpinning new development opportunities with rigorous market intelligence, forward curves, fundamental analysis, scenario modelling and asset-level commercial insight. The initial priority is to establish repeatable capabilities for core markets and then scale them across Northland’s broader international portfolio.

The role is required to work in the Toronto office 4 days per week with one flexible day to work from home.

Key Responsibilities

Market Intelligence

Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, lead the development of Northland’s wholesale market strategy across relevant jurisdictions, identifying long-term trends, structural opportunities, downside risks and implications for capital allocation.
Develop and maintain internal views on supply and demand evolution, market design, natural gas, carbon, capacity, ancillary services, environmental attributes and other material value drivers.
Create a consistent market-outlook and assumption-setting process for use across business cases, investment decisions, budgets, forecasts and commercial strategies.
Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, translate market, policy and regulatory developments into alerts and actionable recommendations for internal stakeholders.

Forecasting, Modelling and Analytics

Own the roadmap and delivery of internal forward curves (short and long term), market-level fundamental models and supporting analytical tools, beginning with priority markets and scaling as business needs and capability mature.
Set modelling architecture, scenarios, input assumptions and quality standards; provide sufficient technical depth to review, challenge and guide Python-based and commercial-platform model development.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analysis covering load growth, generation additions and retirements, fuel and carbon prices, weather, transmission build-out, policy, technology costs, capture rates and operating constraints.
Build dashboards and repeatable reporting that make market views, assumptions, risks and forecast changes transparent and accessible to decision-makers.

Asset, Portfolio and Transaction Decision Support

Lead market analysis supporting development, acquisitions, divestitures, financing, budgeting and optimization of operating assets, including merchant revenue forecasts and high-level asset valuations.
Provide dispatch, capture-price, congestion, basis, curtailment, ancillary-service and other commercial analyses appropriate to each market, technology and contract structure.
Support hedging decisions, PPA and offtake strategy, competitive bid and RFP analysis, route-to-market decisions, commercial operating strategies and portfolio risk discussions.
Partner with Finance and transaction teams on lender, sale and investment processes, using independent third-party forecasts where external validation is required while maintaining a clear Northland view.

Capability, Data and Model Governance

Establish a practical build-versus-buy strategy for data, tools, modelling platforms and external advisory support, with clear accountabilities, budgets and service standards.
Implement model governance covering documentation, version control, assumption ownership, change management, validation, back-testing [CS3.1]and independent challenge proportionate to the decision being supported.
Define data requirements and partner with Technical Performance Management, Data, Digital and IT teams to develop reliable and scalable market-data infrastructure.
Manage relationships with market-data providers, modelling vendors and consultants; reduce avoidable external dependence while retaining specialist support where it adds value or is required by third parties.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnerships

Build, lead and develop a high-performing market intelligence and analytics team, setting priorities and balancing recurring market coverage with transaction and asset-specific demands.
Act as a senior thought partner to Development, Regulatory & Market Affairs, Government Affairs, Asset Management, Risk, Finance and executive leadership.
Present complex market conclusions, model limitations and key uncertainties in a clear, decision-oriented manner for investment committees, senior leaders and boards.

Who You Are

A strategic market leader: You possess deep expertise in wholesale power and commodity markets and can translate market trends, risks and opportunities into commercial strategy, investment decisions and portfolio outcomes. 
An analytical and technically credible expert: You combine strong quantitative capabilities with hands-on experience in market modelling, forecasting and data analytics, bringing the ability to challenge assumptions, interrogate models and drive rigorous decision-making. 
A builder of capabilities: You thrive in creating and scaling new functions, frameworks and governance models, balancing internal capability development with the strategic use of external tools, data and advisory support. 
A trusted advisor and communicator: You can distill complex market dynamics, forecasts and uncertainties into clear, actionable insights that influence executives, investment committees and boards. 
A collaborative and inspiring leader: You build high-performing teams, foster technical excellence and partner effectively across functions, geographies and stakeholder groups to deliver business value. 

Qualifications And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in economics, engineering, mathematics, statistics, finance, computer science or a related discipline; a relevant master’s degree or MBA is an asset.
10 or more years of progressive experience in wholesale power markets, energy-market analytics, fundamental forecasting, commercial strategy or a closely related field, including leadership of people or major analytical programs.
Demonstrated experience developing or directing power-market forecasts, fundamental models, dispatch and revenue analysis, scenario frameworks and asset-valuation inputs.
Deep understanding of electricity-market design and commercial drivers; experience across more than one ISO/RTO or international market is strongly preferred.
Experience across a diverse technology portfolio, such as wind, solar, storage and gas-fired generation, and with contracted and merchant revenue structures.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, manage external advisors and convert complex analytical work into clear commercial decisions.

What’s In It for You:

Our employees are the driving force behind our achievements. We are unwavering in our commitment to not only recognise your contributions but also to empower
you to excel in every aspect of your life. Here's a glimpse of why Northland is the place where you'll truly thrive: 

Thoughtful benefits – A competitive RRSP matching scheme of 8%; extended health, dental and vision benefits for yourself and your immediate family from day one; paid parental leave; Accident and Life Insurance and disability benefits are just a few of the benefits you’ll be able to access. 
Wellbeing first – Staying true to our taking care of ourselves and each other value, you will have access to our global Wellness Program and Employee Assistance Program, including access to mental health resources. 
Floating days and Birthdays off – As part of our commitment to promoting a healthy work-life balance, you will get your birthday off so you can celebrate however you choose! You will also receive three additional days off annually to observe any other events that are important to you.

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we still encourage you to apply. Learn more about our diversity, inclusion and belonging commitments.
